Trump has turned the Department of Justice into his own personal vendetta machine. And Pam Bondi was happy to go along for the ride.

We've witnessed the most egregious politicization of the DOJ in recent memory.

And I lived through the Nixon years.

Reminder that as a corporate lobbyist, Pam Bondi represented scores of clients facing federal regulatory scrutiny — including Amazon, Uber, and GM.

She also represented the government of Qatar and ICE contractor GEO Group.

She was a walking, talking conflict of interest at the DOJ.
Textbook corporate greed.

Trump promised…

His tariffs would revive American manufacturing (we’ve lost manufacturing jobs).

He would lower gas prices (they’re higher than they’ve been in years).

He would keep us out of any new wars (there’s no end in sight for his war on Iran).

Has he kept any of his promises?

-Trump & Kushner have billions in business with the Saudis
-Eric & Don Jr. are backing a drone-manufacturing DoD contractor
-Hegseth's broker tried to invest millions in defense stocks prior to US strikes

Trump's inner circle profits from war while everyone else pays the price.
Textbook corporate greed.

Jeff Bezos' Washington Post editorial board endorsed Pam Bondi as a "qualified" and "serious" pick for Attorney General.

Nowhere in the endorsement did they mention that she's a former Amazon lobbyist.

Another reminder that billionaire control of our media is a threat to democracy.
Trump won't be personally hurt by high gas prices. But you will — and that’s a sacrifice he’s willing to make.

Trump said we “can’t take care of daycare” because “we’re fighting wars.”

Hello? The $200B he wants for his war could provide every child in the country with a free school lunch for a year & have $170 billion to spare.

Trump can help people here at home — he’s just choosing not to.

Trump has turned the Department of Justice into his own personal vendetta machine. And Pam Bondi was happy to go along for the ride.

We've witnessed the most egregious politicization of the DOJ in recent memory.

And I lived through the Nixon years.

Here's the truth about tax cuts for the rich.

They explode the federal debt, fuel giant profits at the biggest firms and financial institutions, and stoke a surge in billionaire wealth but do nothing for average working people. 

Nothing trickles down.

We are spending an estimated $1B per day on the war on Iran.

Now Trump and Co want an extra $200B from Congress to fund the war.

But healthcare? Cut.

Food stamps? Cut.

Education? Cut.

Cancer research? Cut.

Environmental protections? Cut.

And of course, taxes on the rich? Cut.

It's obscene.

One year after Trump's "Liberation Day," where are we? 

He said tariffs would revive U.S. manufacturing, but we lost nearly 100,000 manufacturing jobs in 2025.

Meanwhile, U.S. imports grew while the trade deficit in goods hit a record high.

The chaos amounted to nothing but higher costs for you.
